title: fix(config): surface inaccessible roots during config loads
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Config loading treats an inaccessible root as a missing file: the synchronous existence probe hides read failures, and the asynchronous probe converts every rejection into `false`. OpenClaw can therefore silently load fresh-install defaults instead of reporting an unreadable configuration.

## User Impact

An inaccessible configured root is reported as an I/O failure instead of silently loading unrelated fresh-install defaults. A genuinely missing config retains existing defaults. No configuration or migration action is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

Read the root once. Reuse the existing synchronous reader and apply the same ENOENT-only absence policy asynchronously. Genuine absence retains the existing defaults; other failures reach the existing environment rollback, path-bearing error log, and original-error rethrow. Config validation, includes, recovery, materialization, and public config/SDK/protocol shapes are unchanged.

Production delta: +11/-11, zero net lines. The 64-line regression exercises both actual factory APIs through filesystem faults; it adds no production testing seam.

## Best-effort tradeoffs accepted

- A root disappearing before its single read is ordinary absence. An unavailable root now visibly fails instead of falling back to unrelated defaults. No retry or second existence check is added.
- This completes the established absent-versus-unavailable policy already used by the snapshot reader (#159598). The asynchronous preflight came through #148305; no human permission-error incident is claimed as provenance.

## Evidence

Independent isolated review through P2 is scoped-clean (confidence 0.96), including the complete load/factory/effects/read/context contracts. Source verification, formatting, whitespace, and normal signed commits passed. No timeout, retry, skip, suppression or baseline expansion was added.

Local negative-control execution remained incomplete: the focused two-case suite prepared its cold worker generation in 557.45s, then did not reach an assertion verdict before the task-owned run was intentionally stopped after more than seventeen minutes under shared-host load (exit 130). Its wrapper and owned children fully joined. This is not a reproduced failure, a passing baseline, or evidence of a product fault. Positive runtime and targeted types/lint remain pending; exact-head hosted CI is required. No real operator configuration/state, CLI/Gateway service, live provider or deployment was used.

The mandatory local suppression guard on the exact signed head completed **1 passed / 2 failed** (323.67s Vitest, 398.48s wrapper). One unchanged source-inventory test exceeded its existing120s timeout under shared-host load; no timeout was raised and this is not evidence of a config regression. The other was the unchanged warm-reload probe suppression95 versus allowlist94, already removed on main in `095f94ce98866b3f557daa47be31395e4bc25075`. Neither determining guard/probe source is changed by this two-file PR. No local green, matching-baseline timeout reproduction, or CI waiver is claimed; current exact-head hosted CI remains required. No additional broad local command was selected under the coordinator's explicit budget; the focused wrapper's earlier prerequisite expansion and deliberate stop are reported above.

The first hosted run `38958757226` passed its runtime and type jobs and found an owned `eslint(no-shadow)` in this new regression's access mock. The fix consistently renames that callback parameter to `accessMode`, forwarding exactly the same value; fixtures, assertions and production code are unchanged. Independent P0–P2 review of this correction is scoped-clean (confidence0.99). The failed job log was fetched once; no job was rerun.

On signed correction head `c164dcf5e26fb466a1f40118c573b63ca9b6b609`, focused syntax lint passed. The fresh mandatory suppression guard completed **2 passed / 1 failed** (182.22s Vitest, 267.90s wrapper): the Git inventory check passed; only the unchanged warm-reload suppression95 versus94 mismatch remained, fixed on main by the commit cited above. No guard/baseline/suppression change or repeated run for green was made. Prior-head runtime/type passes remain prior-head evidence; new-head hosted CI is the broad gate.
